classification: Read-only evidence extraction for the current physically booted SD fallback; not independent acceptance

firmware_source_and_configuration.interpretation: Pinned recipe configures a volatile environment and disables the saveenv command and identified misc/system-switch/bootcount/OTA paths. The assembled boot command reads SD files and, on failure, waits; it does not request persistent environment writes.
refs: docs/implementation-evidence.md#Independent boot review (Other-device fallback, Persistent environment, System switching / boot count, Misc command write, Recovery-key misc write, Boot parameters / userdata, Opaque boot0 / monitor)

physical_observations.early_linux_sd_counters: corrected-host-boot evidence states Linux SD write/discard/flush counters are zero; /sys/block/mmcblk1/stat has writes completed=0 and sectors written=0 at the sample
physical_observations.interpretation: Only Linux block-layer activity observed at the recorded early sample; it cannot observe ROM, boot0, monitor, or pre-kernel writes.

limits_and_gaps: The exact boot_package.fex is a vendor-packed binary including opaque firmware. Source/config review constrains known U-Boot writes but does not prove every ROM, boot0, secure monitor, or binary path is side-effect free.
No firmware-level write trace or instrumentation is retained; Linux counters begin after firmware handoff.

A single full-card baseline is not a before/after unchanged-card comparison across repeated boot, workload, shutdown, and restart cycles. The 10 cold/10 warm and sustained zero-SD-write acceptance gate remains open (docs/hypervisor-plan.md:110-117; docs/implementation-status.md#Acceptance requirements and evidence).
No complete physical boot-cycle firmware audit establishes behavior under failed boot, missing NVMe, or recovery paths.

not_current_candidate.note: Do not use the separate unbooted NVMe-first transport SD/package as evidence for this fallback. Current package is b20c3d...; separate candidate has different artifact/config and remains unbooted.

conclusion: Good source/config and early Linux-counter evidence supports the intended immutable fallback policy. It does not yet prove zero routine physical SD writes across the acceptance cycles or rule out opaque pre-kernel firmware writes.
